one_month_reasoning: No AT&T earnings in the window (Q4 results late January; the last ex-dividend was 2026-10-12). Scheduled read-across: Verizon Q3 on 2026-10-26 (it guides phone adds to the top of 750k-1M and promised positive phone net accounts with no free phones), T-Mobile Q3 2026-10-28, Comcast and Charter late October (cable lost 167k-172k broadband subs in Q2 and adds 400k+ mobile lines a quarter; Comcast flagged fiber's $30-40 gig pricing). A strong Verizon volume print with aggressive pricing would weigh on AT&T; cable broadband losses to fiber would help. The unscheduled driver is SpaceX: the stock fell 10.8% on 2026-10-09 (Grain 800 MHz purchase) and 8.0% on 2026-10-23 (Bloomberg: talks for 80,000+ sites); further headlines (FCC review of Grain, a site deal) skew down, a carrier wholesale deal or pushback (SpaceX's own plan uses rooftop small cells, not macro towers) up. After a ~16% fall in two weeks mean reversion and momentum roughly cancel, so we centre at $21.0 with a 9.5% monthly s.d. (slightly above 30%/3.5 = 8.6% for headline risk). Unchanged from round 1: the supervisor found nothing that moves the 1-month view.

reasoning: Round 2 rebuild after the supervisor's review. Facts fixed: fiber stake now +4,058 x 0.9 as an equity adjustment (R63; round 1 had ~$1.7B in net debt); net debt at the horizon re-derived at 145.4B (Q4 FCF ~6B, 68% of FY27 FCF by Oct-23, three dividends, ~$7B/yr buybacks, NCI/preferred, Mexico x0.9); FCF per share on horizon shares (6,385M); postpaid phone base on reported year-end counts (73.4815M); home-internet FY26 average time-weighted for the Lumen subscribers (14.06M), which lowers fiber ARPU to the -4% the company reports. Model deepened: a sixth driver, the AC EBITDA margin, now sets segment EBIT, and the P/E and FCF legs read EPS and FCF computed from the drivers; Legacy is a plain run-off segment (driven revenue 81%). Industry follow-ups (8 searches/fetches): Verizon steering to the top of its 750k-1M phone-add guide with no free phones (TIKR), Comcast blaming fiber's $30-40 gig pricing for its losses, SpaceX's own plan of rooftop small cells rather than macro towers (Wireless Estimator), and FCC rules forcing the upper C-band auction to close by July 2027 (Light Reading). So we moved 2027 wireless ARPU to +1.6% (from +2.0%, a little below the supervisor's +1.75%), 2027 adds to 1.0M, AC EBITDA to +6.0%/+5.25% (inside the guide, below the 9M +7.0% that Lumen flatters), FCF to $18.7B/$20.1B (just under the floors), and added -$5B x 0.35 for C-band. Peers are the supervisor's 12 incumbents on one CY2027E after-lease basis (median 5.52x, 5.98x ex-DT; P/E 10.55x); our 6.0x on our EV is ~5.58x on that basis and 8.0x P/E matches AT&T today. Research target (12m) $22.24 (round 1 $22.31; supervisor $23.29: we are lower on EBITDA and multiples). Scenarios bear $16.31 / base $22.24 / bull $27.51 at 25/50/25 with 17% within-scenario spread; the ladder shrinks the engine's median (~$22.0) toward spot for post-shock momentum and the SpaceX headline skew, median ~$21.6. Not driver-linked: none (all legs read the drivers); constants in the EPS/FCF expressions are listed in inputs_detail.

model_inputs.structure_note: Driver-led telecom build: 6 drivers (postpaid phones, wireless service ARPU, home internet connections, home internet ARPU, AC EBITDA margin, capital investment). Driven revenue (wireless service + equipment + home internet) is 81% of FY2026 revenue (104,928 of 129,181; base residual 0.0%); the engine's driven-segment share reads 91% because AC Business and Other takes its EBIT margin from the AC margin driver (its revenue is plain). Legacy (copper run-off), Latin America (sold Q1 2027) and Corporate are plain segments. Segment EBIT = AC EBITDA margin - 16.0% D&A; capex = capital_investment; the P/E leg's NTM EPS and the FCF leg's NTM FCF per share are computed from the drivers in driver_build.set (other income, interest, NCI/preferred and average shares as constants), so scenario driver moves re-value every leg. Value is carried by NTM EV/EBITDA (0.5), P/E (0.35) and FCF yield (0.15); no DCF (policy). Fiber stake and expected C-band spend are equity adjustments.
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) the fiber stake is carried at the Lumen Mass Markets held-for-sale book value 4,058 x 0.9; R17 says GIP/CPP buy equity in the JV, so AT&T gets a 50% stake, not cash, and once the network sits in the JV AT&T will likely pay it access fees (size undisclosed, not modelled; a downside to AC margin from H2 2027). (2) EV includes $18.0B subsidiary preferred interests and $2.95B preferred stock, so our 6.0x equals ~5.58x on the peers' EV basis. (3) Upper C-band: -$5B x 0.35. (4) We sit below the supervisor's reconciled set on 2027 wireless ARPU (+1.6% vs +1.75%), adds (1.0M vs 1.1M), AC EBITDA (+6.0%/+5.25% vs +6.25%/+6.0%) and the multiples (6.0x/8.0x vs 6.1x/8.2x) on the industry evidence (Verizon volume push, cable fiber price war, SpaceX service start at the horizon).
